answer_1.quote: Transformer-based pretrained language models (LMs) have led to a wave of advances in natural language generation tasks
datasets: Jigsaw Toxic Comment Classification Challenge Dataset

answer_2.quote: We evaluate our generated outputs for toxicity, fluency and diversity. Following previous evaluation methods, we characterize generation toxicity with the toxicity score given by Perpective API

answer_4.quote: we carry out human evaluation on toxicity and fluency of generated text to compare baselines with our method. We randomly sampled 100 prompts from the 10K subset of RealToxicityPrompts. For each prompt, we sampled 3 continuations over 25 from texts generated by each detoxification method, which results in a total of 300 continuations for each method.
answer_4.guideline: Each continuation is evaluated by two annotators, who rate fluency on a scale of 1 to 5 (1 being very confused and 5 being very fluent) and rate toxicity on a scale of 0 to 2 (0 being nontoxic at all, 1 being mildly toxic and 2 being toxic).
